verdict_reason: Both estimands are implemented exactly and both are emitted under distinct names. The rowwise kernel (positional_decay.py:29-56) matches an independent tie-averaged rank-then-Pearson reference over 300 rows with ties injected in one third of them at a maximum absolute difference of 1.11e-16; the manuscript's pooled kernel (positional_decay.py:192-237, every causal {i,j} pair from q=1 with the diagonal, exactly as sections/metrics_geometry.tex:246-251 writes it) matches the same independent reference over 50 randomised causal heads at 5.55e-17. The headline `mean_positional_decay_correlation` is deliberately the ROWWISE mean, and I measured this to settle the estimand dispute rather than argue it: the CODE IS RIGHT AND THE PAPER SHOULD CHANGE. (1) On an exactly uniform causal attention pattern -- no positional preference by construction -- the pooled statistic reads -0.4344766895 (L=8), -0.4571393525 (16), -0.4659740104 (64), -0.4664886660 (128), -0.4666215371 (256) against a correct 0, while the rowwise reads EXACTLY 0.0 at every length. (2) The objection that the rowwise 0.0 is merely its constant-row convention does not survive: on an iid-random causal null (every row an independent Dirichlet-flat probability vector, so every row has genuine spread and the constant-row branch never fires) the pooled mean over 20 heads is -0.2492045178 at L=64 (sd 0.0160) and -0.2447022421 at L=256 (sd 0.0041), while the rowwise mean is +0.0039036484 and +0.0031867344 -- rowwise is null-calibrated to within 0.004, pooled carries a -0.245 offset. (3) The rowwise is not merely insensitive, it is MORE sensitive: on an exp(-0.3d) decaying head it reads exactly -1.0000000000 where pooled reads -0.9997312664 (L=64), and on a head whose attention GROWS with distance it reads exactly +1.0000000000 where pooled reads only +0.4493801081 -- the pooled statistic's range is asymmetric and cannot reach +1 because of the same mask bias. (4) On a real bf16 gpt2 promoted to fp32 with eager attention the pooled value is -0.4719692460839507 against a uniform-causal null of -0.4666215371 at the same L=256 truncation, i.e. 98.9% of the manuscript's statistic is causal-mask geometry and only -0.0053 is attributable to the model; the rowwise headline is -0.2593986643038708.
comparable_reason: Not comparable as shipped, for reasons that are entirely configuration and protocol, not implementation. defaults.yaml:85-86 sets num_samples = 5 and the code truncates at 256 tokens (positional_decay.py:117), against a metric whose stated purpose is long-context positional integrity; the five default WikiText-103 passages are 157/154/83/71/62 GPT-2 tokens, so 3 of 5 never reach 128 and 0 of 5 reach 256. The rowwise statistic is length-dependent by construction (a q-token row has only q keys), so two models tokenising the same corpus into different numbers of tokens are compared on different row-length distributions. The task is absent from all 66 archived result files at git 33743e8, so I could not measure a cross-model architecture correlation on the archive at all. The pooled twin is strictly worse on this axis: its -0.2447 to -0.4666 null offset is a function of context length, so it varies with tokenizer granularity independent of any model property. `_meta_attention_sink_mass` is emitted, which is the right disclosure, and sink mass ranges 14.5-47.3% across models per the module docstring -- a model-dependent, non-cancelling component of the raw number.
github_reason: No code was ever released for this metric, and there is no upstream to fetch: the module cites only "2024-2025 Long-Context Extrapolation and RoPE literature" and the BLME manuscript's own equation. RoFormer (Su et al.) releases code for the ROTATION, not for a rank correlation between attention mass and key distance; ALiBi (Press et al.) releases a bias term and measures extrapolation by perplexity, not by rho. I therefore built two independent references myself -- a tie-averaged rank-then-Pearson Spearman and an independent causal-pair enumeration -- and both branches of BLME agree with them to 1.11e-16 (rowwise, 300 rows, ties in 1/3) and 5.55e-17 (pooled, 50 randomised causal heads). NONE here is the honest and useful answer, not a gap in the review.
paper_reason: No published scalar exists anywhere in this chain to reproduce. The BLME manuscript's positional-decay subsection (sections/metrics_geometry.tex:246-251) contains one defining equation and zero result values; RoFormer plots a decay curve of an upper BOUND on the inner product, not a rank correlation on trained attention; ALiBi plots perplexity against extrapolation length. What IS reproducible is the analytic null, and the shipped headline reproduces it exactly: a uniform causal pattern must give 0, and the rowwise gives 0.0000000000 at L = 8, 16, 64, 128 and 256, while the manuscript's own estimand gives -0.4344766895 to -0.4666215371 on the identical fixtures.
confounds_reason: Confirmed as a structural confound with CONTEXT LENGTH and tokenizer granularity rather than with d_model or n_layers, and confirmed by construction rather than by fit. The pooled twin's null offset is a monotone function of L alone: -0.4344766895 at L=8 rising to -0.4666215371 at L=256 on an attention pattern that contains no model at all. The rowwise headline has no such offset (0.0 at every L), but it is still averaged over rows whose lengths are set by how the model's own tokenizer splits the shared corpus. The sink component is separately confirmed and model-dependent: the module records sink mass 47.3% (gpt2), 41.3% (distilgpt2), 14.5% (pythia-70m), and position 0 is simultaneously the sink and the maximum-distance key in every causal row, so it enters the correlation at the far end of the very range being measured. I could not measure rho against d_model / n_layers / params because the task is present in 0 of the 66 archived files.
defects: PAPER (not code): sections/metrics_geometry.tex:246-251 defines the POOLED Spearman, which the measurement above shows is not null-calibrated (-0.4666215371 at L=256, and -0.2447 on an iid-random causal null where the rowwise convention never fires, both against a correct 0). The code's rowwise headline is the correct estimand and the manuscript must be reconciled to it. This is the one case in this campaign where the code is right and the paper is wrong.

CONFIG defaults.yaml:85-86: num_samples = 5 for a metric whose stated subject is long-context positional integrity, with a 256-token truncation; the shipped five passages are 157/154/83/71/62 GPT-2 tokens, so none reaches the truncation length and the long-context claim is untested by the shipped configuration.

CODE/POLICY positional_decay.py:104-107: the fp32 promotion is skipped above 2,000,000,000 parameters, which makes the value discontinuous in a reported parameter count rather than in anything measured. The brief excludes dtype coverage from the verdict axis and the promotion itself is correct and necessary (bf16 makes 20.88% of pythia-70m rows exactly flat), but above the cutoff the task silently reports a bf16 number under the same key as an fp32 one. Either fail closed above the cutoff or emit the promotion state as a gate rather than only as `_meta_promoted_to_fp32`.

CODE (latent, not reproduced) positional_decay.py:109-110,239-242: `model.float()` converts floating-point BUFFERS as well as parameters, but the `finally` block restores only parameters. I tested this end to end on a bf16 gpt2 and found the model fully restored -- 0 parameters and 0 buffers changed dtype -- because gpt2's buffers are bool/int. It remains a latent cross-task hazard on an architecture carrying float buffers, and the restore loop should iterate `named_buffers()` too.

DOMAIN GAP (documentation): the pooled branch runs on q >= 1 with the diagonal included while the rowwise runs on q >= 3 with the diagonal excluded, so the two emitted keys differ by an estimand change AND a domain change at once. On real gpt2 I measure -0.2593986643 rowwise against -0.4719692460 pooled; the manuscript should state the exact causal domain so a reader can separate the two contributions.
MISSING OUTPUT: there is no per-layer pooled map (`layer_positional_decay` exists only for the rowwise branch), so the estimand gap cannot be inspected by depth.
